# OVERVIEW

StRyKr Ai is an applied intelligence firm. We remove the operational constraints that block growth — broken workflows, preventable revenue loss, and shortages of workforce capacity — and build measurable systems to address them.

Engagements are led by the principals accountable for the recommendation. Where the work requires engineering, education, healthcare, economic analysis, legal, immigration, securities, credentialing, or community expertise, the relevant specialist is identified before the engagement begins.

No borrowed credibility. No invented outcomes.

# AI AUTOMATIONS & CUSTOM AGENTS

StRyKr Ai finds the repetitive operational work draining hours from your team — then builds automations with permissions, business rules, review gates, monitoring, and rollback, measured against a baseline agreed before a line of code is written.

Operating principle: One defined problem · One accountable owner · One baseline · A scale-or-stop decision at every stage.

## Constraints Addressed
- Time lost in workflows
- Revenue lost between systems
- Capacity lost to workforce gaps

## Outcomes Delivered
- Faster cycle time
- Protected revenue
- Greater service capacity
- Traceable decisions

## Operating Layer
Diagnose → Design → Govern → Integrate → Measure

## Four Entry Points

### 01 — Intake & Re-keying
Stop typing the same record twice. Requests arrive by email and form, then staff re-enter the same information into two or three systems with no reliable view of what has stalled.
First deliverable: One documented workflow with a time baseline, automation architecture, review points, and implementation estimate.

### 02 — Classification & Routing
Send each case to the right owner, first time. Triage depends on tenure and memory. Misrouted work is discovered late, and exception handling is invisible to the people accountable for it.
First deliverable: Routing rule set with confidence thresholds, human review queue, and exception reporting.

### 03 — Follow-up & Escalation
Close the gap where value leaks out. Renewals, unbilled work, and stalled cases depend on someone remembering. Nobody owns the follow-up, so revenue quietly ages out.
First deliverable: Quantified opportunity register validated with finance and the operational owner.

### 04 — Custom AI Agents
Task-specific agents, on approved knowledge only. Employees cannot reliably find approved knowledge or complete multistep work across systems without leaving the sanctioned path.
First deliverable: Agent charter — approved sources, permissions, tools, escalation, evaluation, and release criteria.

## Five Governance Pillars (aligned to NIST AI RMF)
1. Permissions — Role-based access to systems and data, defined before build.
2. Business rules — Explicit boundaries on what the system may recommend or change.
3. Review gates — A named human owner for every consequential decision.
4. Monitoring — Audit record of request, context, output, reviewer, and resolution.
5. Rollback — An accessible off switch and a documented path back.

# AI FOR EDUCATION (K-12 & HIGHER ED)

Give your K-12 & Higher Ed administrators and educators more capacity to serve. Institutions are being asked to adopt AI faster than governance can absorb it. We build the guardrails first, then the capability, so adoption does not create a compliance problem later.

## AI Training & Policy Snapshot (External Evidence)
- 50% of teachers report no AI training
- 28-point training gap by district poverty level
- 45% of principals report any AI policy

Training gap by district poverty:
- Low poverty (<25%): 56% trained
- Moderate (25–75%): 38% trained
- High poverty (>75%): 28% trained

## Role-Specific Training Programs

### K-12 Teachers
Problem: Teachers are using AI for planning, differentiation, and feedback — usually with tools nobody vetted. Without training, student data ends up in unapproved systems and grading decisions lose their paper trail.
Agent built: Lesson-planning and differentiation assistant grounded in district curriculum map and IEP accommodations — drafts only, never a submitted grade.
Benchmark: 5.9 hrs/week reported saved (Gallup/Walton, 2025)
Coverage: Approved tool list, student data boundaries, prompting for lesson design, feedback vs. grading, detector limitations, disclosure to families
Guardrails: No student-identifiable data leaves approved tools; AI-assisted feedback is labeled; grades of record require teacher authorship

### School Administrators
Problem: Administrators field parent questions, vendor pitches, and staff requests with no shared approval process.
Agent built: Vendor-review and policy-drafting assistant.
Benchmark: 3.2 hrs/week reported saved
Coverage: Vendor intake checklist, data-sharing agreement review, staff request triage, family communication templates

### Principals
Problem: Principals are accountable for how AI touches grading, discipline, and family communication but can't see where staff are already using it.
Agent built: Building-level adoption dashboard.
Benchmark: 41% faster incident response

### District Leadership
Problem: District leaders own the policy and public risk but inherit a patchwork of building-level decisions.
Agent built: District-wide policy and risk-register assistant.
Benchmark: 3 fewer unresolved exceptions per quarter

### Counselors & Advisors
Problem: Counselors use AI for scheduling and recommendation drafting — high-stakes work where errors follow students for years.
Agent built: Drafting assistant for recommendation letters and intervention notes.
Benchmark: 4.1 hrs/week reported saved

### IT & Information Security
Problem: IT is asked to secure tools already in use before the department knew about them.
Agent built: Access-and-audit console mapping AI tools through SSO.
Benchmark: 62% fewer unmanaged tool instances

### Higher-Ed Faculty
Problem: Faculty redesign assignments without institutional guidance on acceptable AI use.
Agent built: Assignment-redesign assistant with process-evidence-based assessment structures.
Benchmark: 2x faster assignment redesign

## Institutional Self-Assessment (8 statements)
1. We have a written, published policy on student and staff AI use.
2. Every employee has completed foundational AI literacy and data-privacy training.
3. Staff can correctly say which data may enter which approved tool.
4. Consequential decisions — grading, discipline, eligibility, aid — have documented human authority.
5. AI tools are reached through SSO with role-based permissions and audit logs.
6. Our AI-facing tools have been tested against WCAG 2.1 AA.
7. Assessments have been redesigned around process evidence rather than detector scores.
8. Every AI pilot has a baseline, an owner, subgroup measures, and a go/no-go date.

Scoring levels: Exposed (0-5), Developing (6-10), Structured (11-15), Governed (16)

# WORKFORCE & EB-5 PROJECT READINESS

Build the capacity required to grow responsibly. StRyKr Ai coordinates employer demand, workforce forecasting, credentialing, candidate pathways, project readiness, disclosure, and the independent professionals required for regulated processes.

## Healthcare Workforce Practice
A reliable view of demand, pipeline, and risk. Employers rarely hold one picture of role-and-site demand, credential milestones, onboarding status, and retention risk.
Services:
- Role-and-site workforce forecast
- Credentialing operating model with milestone owners
- Ethical recruitment standards and candidate disclosure
- Onboarding and retention risk reporting

Market context: 1.9M healthcare openings projected per year, on average, from 2024 through 2034 (U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, 2025).

## EB-5 Project Readiness Practice
Documentation, disclosure, and defined professional roles. Project information, professional responsibilities, and publication controls are usually fragmented across parties.
Services:
- Readiness register of documents and owners
- Unresolved-question log with escalation path
- Publication controls before any public claim
- Coordination with independent licensed professionals

Illustrative readiness register items:
- Project business plan and job-creation methodology → Economist (independent)
- Offering documents and disclosure package → Securities counsel
- Immigration eligibility and filing strategy → Immigration counsel
- Construction and site readiness evidence → Project sponsor
- Public claim and marketing review → StRyKr Ai coordination

## Boundary Note
StRyKr Ai provides information, readiness, operational coordination, and documentation standards. Legal, immigration, securities, licensure, and investment determinations remain with the appropriate licensed professionals and government agencies. USCIS administers the EB-5 program and determines immigration eligibility and adjudication. StRyKr Ai does not guarantee immigration outcomes, visa availability, or investment returns.

# ABOUT StRyKr Ai

Senior by design. Specialist by need.

## Five Principles
1. Business case before build — establish the cost of the current state, the decision owner, and the target measure before recommending technology.
2. Production over presentation — prototypes are tested against real cases, users, and exceptions. A demonstration is not a deployment.
3. Human authority stays visible — escalation, approval, override, and deactivation are designed before launch — not retrofitted.
4. Designed for existing operations — systems are built around the tools, permissions, policies, and teams that must operate them.
5. Evidence before expansion — every release has a baseline, monitoring plan, decision date, and criteria to scale, revise, or stop.

## Engagement Process
Phase 01 — Discover: Map the workflow, systems, data, people, exceptions, risks, and current cost. Gate: Is the problem material, measurable, and suitable for StRyKr Ai?
Phase 02 — Design: Future workflow, architecture, ownership, controls, integration, and measurement method. Gate: Does expected value justify the cost, effort, and risk?
Phase 03 — Deploy: One bounded release against real cases, with named reviewers, monitoring, and rollback. Gate: Is performance reliable enough to remain live or expand?
Phase 04 — Measure: Compare with the agreed baseline — value, quality, adoption, exception rates, and risk. Gate: Scale, revise, transfer, or stop?

## Evidence Standard
Every published outcome includes:
- Baseline: what was happening before the intervention
- Scope: the workflow, site, population, or period measured
- Result: the observed change, including unfavorable findings
- Source: the system or institution the measure came from
- Validation: the client owner or independent party that reviewed it
- Limits: what the result does not establish

## Team
- Principal — Applied AI: workflow diagnosis, solution architecture, deployment governance
- Principal — Revenue Intelligence: leakage quantification, controls design, finance validation
- Practice Lead — Workforce: demand forecasting, credentialing operations, employer coordination
- Named collaborators: legal, immigration, securities, or clinical specialists, engaged per scope

Names, roles, credentials, licenses, partnerships, client references, and collaborator relationships appear publicly only after confirmation. StRyKr Ai's AI governance method is aligned to — not certified by — the NIST AI Risk Management Framework.
